name: Teleporters (Hard Version)
description: The only difference between the easy and hard versions are the locations you can teleport to. Consider the points $$$0,1,\dots,n+1$$$ on the number line. There is a teleporter located on each of the points $$$1,2,\dots,n$$$. At point $$$i$$$, you can do the following: Move left one unit: it costs $$$1$$$ coin. Move right one unit: it costs $$$1$$$ coin. Use a teleporter at point $$$i$$$, if it exists: it costs $$$a_i$$$ coins. As a result, you can choose whether to teleport to point $$$0$$$ or point $$$n+1$$$. Once you use a teleporter, you can't use it again. You have $$$c$$$ coins, and you start at point $$$0$$$. What's the most number of teleporters you can use?
input_specification: The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 1000$$$) — the number of test cases. The descriptions of the test cases follow. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$c$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 2\cdot10^5$$$; $$$1 \leq c \leq 10^9$$$)  — the length of the array and the number of coins you have respectively. The following line contains $$$n$$$ space-separated positive integers $$$a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the costs to use the teleporters. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2\cdot10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output the maximum number of teleporters you can use.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1791G2 — Teleporters (Hard Version) [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
